chunks: Abd al-Walid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Naysaburi al-Attar (RA) said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah al-Naysaburi said, on the authority of Hamdan ibn Sulayman that I wrote to al-Rida (AS) asking him whether the actions of the servants are created or uncreated?
So he (AS) wrote back, “The actions of the servants were decreed through the Knowledge of Allah, the Might and High, two thousand years before the creation of the servants.”
ai.seo_question: Are human actions created by God or uncreated according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Hamdan ibn Sulayman inquires whether human actions are created (*makhluq*) or uncreated (*ghayr makhluq*). Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that while the specific acts are pre-decreed in Divine Knowledge two thousand years prior to creation, this affirms the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), balancing divine omniscience with human agency. This response avoids the extremes of absolute determinism (*jabr*) and total free will (*tafriy*), establishing a nuanced theological framework for understanding predestination.
